source.citation: Haas, Kevin. Earth two-track through sagebrush steppe. Photograph, 26 June 2021. Owner's own work, supplied for this project 2026-08-15.
what_it_does_not_supply: tallgrass prairie - it is sagebrush steppe, pale Artemisia and bunchgrass on dry ground; the earth-against-vegetation contrast here is LOWER than deep-green July tallgrass would give, so any threshold derived from it is conservative and must be labelled so
the flat lake plain - the ground is rolling, so a horizon here is a ridge line rather than the true horizon Chicago's sightlines have
a location - the file carries no GPS and none is asserted
wagon-road width - this is a single-vehicle two-track; an 1835 street was a platted corridor about ten metres wide, and only the surface contrast transfers
a reuse licence - it is committed so a reader can CHECK the figures against it, and that is all. All rights reserved by the owner; no redistribution, republication or derived asset.
what_it_supplies: the fall of earth-track contrast with distance, from underfoot to the horizon, at a resolution that resolves the track in every band the road gate scores
a direct digital capture whose absolute sRGB is not mediated by film, print or scanner, unlike the Kansas scan
a frame model: 26 mm equivalent over 3024 px = 57.0 px/deg, the same lens geometry as the sky reference, so elevation per pixel is computable once the horizon row is found
a date five days from the scene date, 26 June against 1 July
